text: A short distance to the west of Kirkjuhóll (Church Knoll) there is another small hill called Hulduhóll (the knoll of the hidden people). Excavations at Hulduhóll indicate that the knoll was partially man-made. On top of this knoll the archaeologists uncovered a cremation dating from around A.D. 1000. This grave contained the burned bones of a man in 40s along with fragments of iron and bronze artifacts. This is the first cremation grave yet uncovered in Iceland and provides an important contribution to our knowledge of the pagan religion and the variation in burial traditions in early Iceland.
